profile.diet: Sea urchins, sand dollars, crabs, and mollusks
profile.behavior: Strong-jawed reef fish that builds shallow nests in sand near reefs and feeds on hard-shelled invertebrates.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, favorable for triggerfish.
factors.value_notes: A 2026 Florida Panhandle tag-return analysis of 3,744 released gray triggerfish recorded capture SST of 15–31 °C (median 22 °C) and reported lower recapture proportions with increasing SST, especially above 20 °C. A southeastern U.S. spawning survey recorded spawning females at 15–27 °C (mean 22.7 °C). These are release/recapture and spawning observations, not a validated habitat-preference curve or local South Florida catch optimum; they do not directly validate 18–28 °C / 21–26 °C.

NOAA and Florida Museum describe adults using natural/artificial reefs, hardbottom, ledges, and seaward reefs; juveniles and some adults associate with Sargassum. The sources support reef/hardbottom use but do not validate wreck preference or the exact numeric category ranking.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in reef depth zone.
factors.value_notes: NOAA reports adult depth around 10–55 m and Florida Museum reports reef habitat to about 55 m; the 2026 Florida Panhandle tag-return dataset sampled 20–67 m. These observations support a mid-depth reef association but do not validate the configured 10–100 m outer band or 15–50 m ideal. Depth is an active gate.

text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
